transcript:
```plaintext
[doctor] Hi Mr. Cortez, how are you doing today?

[patient] Hello, doctor. I'm not doing too well, actually. I've been feeling really tired and dizzy for the past few weeks.

[doctor] Hmm, I'm sorry to hear that. Can you tell me more about what's been going on?

[patient] Sure. It's been about three weeks now. Every day, I feel tired, dizzy, and sometimes I get nauseous. It's really affecting my work and daily tasks.

[doctor] That sounds tough. How often do you experience the dizziness?

[patient] It happens about 2-3 times a day, and it's really frustrating. I just can't seem to get anything done.

[doctor] I understand. How about your sleep? Are you getting enough rest?

[patient] Not really. I probably get around 6 hours of sleep a night, but it's often disturbed.

[doctor] Okay. And what about your diet? What do you usually eat?

[patient] My diet isn't great, to be honest. I eat a lot of processed foods and not many fruits or vegetables.

[doctor] Do you exercise regularly?

[patient] No, not really. I know I should, but I just haven't been able to get into a routine.

[doctor] I see. Do you smoke or consume alcohol?

[patient] I smoke about 5 cigarettes a day, and I drink socially, maybe 4-5 drinks a week. I don't use any recreational drugs.

[doctor] Thank you for sharing that. It helps me understand your situation better. Now, let's review your medical history. You have prediabetes and hypertension, correct?

[patient] Yes, that's right. I've been following my treatment regimen, but I don't feel any improvement.

[doctor] Alright, Mr. Cortez. I'll make sure we address that as well. Have you experienced any chest pain, palpitations, or swelling in your legs?

[patient] No, none of that.

[doctor] How about shortness of breath, cough, or wheezing?

[patient] No, I haven't had any of those symptoms either.

[doctor] Any vomiting, diarrhea, or constipation?

[patient] No, just occasional nausea.

[doctor] Have you noticed any headaches, seizures, or any other neurological issues?

[patient] No, just the dizziness.

[doctor] Alright. How about joint pain or swelling?

[patient] No, I haven't had any joint pain or swelling.

[doctor] And how are you feeling emotionally? Are the symptoms affecting your mood?

[patient] I'm really frustrated and anxious because of all this. It's been hard to deal with.

[doctor] I can imagine. Let's take a look at your vital signs. Your blood pressure is 140/88 mmHg, heart rate is 78 bpm, respiratory rate is 16 breaths per minute, and your temperature is 98.6 °F. Your oxygen saturation is 98% on room air.

[patient] Okay.

[doctor] Now, I'll conduct a physical examination. I'll start with your heart. [Examines heart] Your heart has a regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs. Next, I'll check your lungs. [Examines lungs] Your lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally.

[patient] Alright.

[doctor] Let's check your neurological status. [Performs neurological exam] You are alert and oriented, no focal deficits. I'll also check your abdomen. [Palpates abdomen] Your abdomen is soft, non-tender, no hepatosplenomegaly. And lastly, I'll check your musculoskeletal system. [Performs musculoskeletal exam] Normal range of motion, no tenderness.

[patient] Okay.

[doctor] We are still awaiting the results of your biochemistry panel, including glucose, electrolytes, and renal and liver function tests. Once we have those results, we can get a clearer picture.

[patient] I hope it helps. I'm just tired of feeling this way.

[doctor] I understand, Mr. Cortez. In the meantime, I'll advise you to increase your fluid intake to ensure adequate hydration.

[patient] Sure, I can do that.

[doctor] I also recommend that you keep a symptom diary. Note any changes in your symptoms, as it will help us in monitoring your condition.

[patient] Okay, I'll start doing that.

[doctor] I am going to refer you to Dr. Karen Liu, an endocrinologist, for further evaluation of potential underlying endocrine or metabolic causes.

[patient] Alright, I can do that.

[doctor] We will need to schedule a follow-up visit in one week to review your lab results and reassess your symptoms.

[patient] Sounds good.

[doctor] Additionally, I want to educate you on the importance of a balanced diet, regular exercise, and smoking cessation. These changes can significantly improve your health and well-being.

[patient] I know I need to make changes. It's just hard to start.

[doctor] I understand. We can provide resources for dietary changes and smoking cessation support to help you get started.

[patient] That would be helpful, thank you.

[doctor] You're welcome. Do you have any questions or concerns right now?

[patient] Not at the moment. I just hope I start feeling better soon.

[doctor] We'll work together to get you there, Mr. Cortez. Remember to follow up in one week or sooner if your symptoms worsen.

[patient] Alright, I will. Thanks, doctor.

[doctor] You're welcome. Take care, and see you soon.
```
